title.narrative: BEST (Beda and Setara: Different yet Equal): Program for Empowering Youth and Religious Actors to promote Tolerance and Diversity. JANUARY - DECEMBER 2023

description.narrative: Religious Leader, Youth Leader, government, local CSO, and public.
The goal of this project is cultivating an inclusive and tolerant society founded on a strong constitutional paradigm in ensuring freedom of religion and beliefs.

This annual narrative report covers activities from January 1 to December 31, 2023. Program activities in 2023 will emphasize the roles of youth and religious leaders who are agents of change in society, they will facilitate dialogue across religious groups, build their credibility in working with networks to promote tolerance and diversity, and build engagement with multi-stakeholder in advocacy work. This activity has started in the final quarter of 2022 and will continue throughout 2023. Activity under Outcome #1: 1) Capacity building of networking and advocacy for Youth and Religious leader. 2) Mentoring for communities. Activity under Outcome #2: 1) Local and national forum to set up a strategy and agenda for local networks. 2) Interfaith dialogue at the local level. Activity under Outcome #3: 1) Stakeholder Forum at the local level. 2) Consultation meeting with stakeholder of government and non-government to build their commitment to strengthening policies and public education on FoRB rights. Activity under Outcome #4: 1) Campaign Content about Different yet Equal through public space. 2) study on the policy of FoRB and dissemination through discussions, writing a policy paper, press conferences, and seminars. Monitoring and Evaluation, The MTR aimed to determine how far the program has progressed in achieving its objectives, its supporting and inhibiting factors, as well as drawing lessons learned as a basis for recommendations for continued program implementation. The evaluation was carried out using the Outcome Mapping, Outcome Harvesting, and Ecological System Theory framework using document reviews, workshops, FGDs, and interviews to collect data and validate changes (outcome statements) reported in program documents.

title.narrative: Social media campaign to achieve strong narrative and messages on FoRB and religious moderation through public space.

description.narrative: In pursuit of mainstreaming the paradigm of Freedom of Religion and Belief (FoRB) within the Indonesian sociopolitical landscape, our campaign in 2023 was strategically designed and executed. YBAW assembled a team with specialized skills to produce and disseminate content. Leveraging the Gusdurian Network’s social media channels, including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, we distributed content under the hashtag #BedaSetara. Our campaign began with research on diverse issues of social media. Concurrently, actual issues were linked to our developing narrative of “BedaSetara.” Building upon previous campaigns, 2023 strategy focused on mainstreaming issues and developing alternative narratives.

comment.narrative: Content in the form of writing, memes, graphics, videos, or social media posting produced by youth groups, religious actors, to promote constitutional paradigms on FoRB and religious moderation.

actual.value: Social media user

comment.narrative:
Throughout 2023, our team produced 48 pieces of content including carousels (8), infographics (6), memes (1), quotes (14), videos (15), greetings (3), and threads (6). Our content reached 2,482,338 individuals with an engagement of 206,220 interactions.
The content for the FoRB campaign in 2023 covered a variety of important topics:
• We highlighted Gus Dur’s story, emphasizing his commitment to championing minority rights and religious freedom. • We shared messages about equality, stressing the importance of treating everyone fairly and equally. • We commemorated religious holidays, using them as opportunities to promote values of tolerance and understanding among different religious communities. • We included advice from respected religious leaders, who shared insights on diversity and equality. • We also added some lighthearted humor from Gus Dur, making discussions about equality more engaging and accessible. • Finally, we used the Gusdurian social media platform to share content from diversity workshops, aiming to educate and inspire people to embrace diversity and equality in their lives.

title.narrative: Interfaith Dialogue at The Local Level

description.narrative: Interfaith dialogues were conducted for the establishment of space for interfaith interaction to build social trust and awareness of FoRB. Dialogues were designed in various formats that adapt to locality and targets, such as discussions about certain local issues, visits between religious groups, and cultural performances. In the period from October to December 2023, young leaders and religious figures in various regions who are connected to the GUSDURian Network have initiated meetings between religious groups in their respective regions. Interfaith dialogue implemented in 7 (seven) locations on 3 regions: Jombang (East Java), Bantul (Yogyakarta), Samarinda (Kalimantan), Pemalang (Central Java), Sumenep (East Java), Pamekasan (East Java), and Solo (Central Java).

actual.value: Representatives of Local GUSDURian Communities, CSO, Representatives of Youth and Religious Leader

comment.narrative:
The forum was held on 24-26 November 2023 at Wisma Hijau, Depok, West Java, presenting 261 representatives of Local GUSDURian Communities, CSO, Representatives of Youth and Religious Leader. This forum divides discussions into three commissions: Organization, Program, and Recommendations. The Organizational Commission, discussed how to build a solid network ecosystem, strengthen networks and advocacy. Apart from that, the forum discussed systematic community advocacy, building R&D within the network, building a resource raising system, and a code of conduct for the network.
Discussions in the program commission, discussed four main issues: 1) tolerant and inclusive society; 2) honest, fair and dignified elections; 3) Tackling the climate crisis; 4) inclusive education. Meanwhile, the Recommendations Commission discussed and designed the recommendations for several issued from this national meeting.
All discussion results are documented in a separate paper and experiences regarding advocacy regarding cases of diversity issues from various regions have also been compiled in a learning book.

The forum discussed three major sins: intolerance, bullying, and sexual violence in the educational environment. 3 (three) approaches need to be taken in responding to this issue. First, at the family level, the way parents educate their children currently cannot be compared to the way they taught them in the past, especially now when children find it easier to find information. The discussion highlighted freedom of religion and belief in Cirebon. The educational aspect is one of the causes of the emergence of intolerant attitudes, so it is necessary to introduce religious moderation from an early age, especially in educational institutions. From this meeting, the Ahmadiyah Congregation group admitted that until now they were still carrying out their worship in secret because the village government did not allow their place of worship to be used. comment.narrative: The forum was held on December 21 2023 at Nahdlatul Ulama University, Pasuruan. This forum began with a plan to create a module to prevent the three major educational sins, which was a follow-up to last year’s national forum, which agreed on inclusive education as a strategic issue. The forum encourages the need for parents to work together to provide education to prevent and handle the three major educational sins: bullying, sexual violence and intolerance. Interfaith community organizations must play a role in spreading the message of preventing the three major sins. GUSDURian will design a module for preventing and handling sexual violence in schools. comment.narrative: The forum was held on November 29 2023 at the South Sulawesi Balitbang Office, Makassar, Sulawesi. The discussion invited multi-stakeholders and religious leaders to accommodate the rights of people with disabilities, especially in accessing education and places of worship that are more disability-friendly. title.narrative: Sub-activity: Mentoring for Youth and Religious Leader

description.narrative:
This activity is part of capacity building for religious leaders and youth leaders as agents of change in 6 regions: West Java, Yogyakarta, Central Java, East Java, Kalimantan and Sulawesi. This activity aims to increase their capacity in community organizing, building networks, and advocating for FoRB issues. This mentoring brings together youth and religious leaders who are alumni of workshop training with Gusdurian community leaders and activists from network organizations in the region.
In the initial stage, GUSDURian has held a workshop for prospective facilitators on 25-27 August 2023 in Yogyakarta which was attended by 32 participants.
The learning process that youth and religious leaders went through during mentoring is as follows: 1. The first stage, analyze the situation using the Scenario Thinking method. 2. In the second stage, participants are invited to discuss to gather information and develop a sustainable agenda using the 3R (Resilience, Respect, Right). 3. In the third stage, participants are invited to map stakeholders at the regional level who will be invited to collaborate and carry out their agendas. 4. The fourth stage, formulate an action plan that will be implemented using the community canvas model.

location.ref: West Java, Yogyakarta, Central Java, East Java, Kalimantan and Sulawesi

comment.narrative: Mentoring activities were initially designed to be held 10 times in 6 provinces (West Java, Central Java, Yogyakarta, East Java, West Kalimantan, and Sulawesi), bringing together participants between regions in meetings. However, to optimize the network mapping process and work agenda, GUSDURian designed the implementation at the district level by delegating more facilitators to be able to reach more districts.

title.narrative: Sub-activity: Workshop Training on Networking and Advocacy for Religious and Youth Leader on West Java

description.narrative:
This activity aims to increase the capacity of young leaders in networking and advocacy. Before implementation, GUSDURian Network held a workshop with 12 prospective facilitators on 24-26 February 2023 in Yogyakarta.
Each workshop that is held goes through the stages indicated: Segment I: Strengthening the Will of Social Leaders. Segment II: Leaders’ Perspectives on Diversity Issues Segment III: Analysis of Sosial Justice. Segment IV: Sosial Justice Perspective. Segment V: Sharing of Best Practice on Advocacy. Segment VI: Exploring Social Justice in Diversity Issues. Segment VII: Reflective Structure Dialogue. Segment VIII: Lobbying and Negotiations.

comment.narrative: This activity will be held in 6 locations. The location of activity implementation in Bandung. There will be 20 youth leader participants and 20 religious leader participants from the area target group on West Java. The YBAW team will prepare modules and facilitators for this training.

target.value: Youth and Religious Leader

comment.narrative: The participants for this training are 20 youth leaders and 20 religious leaders. The religious and youth leaders increased their skills in lobbying, planning, communicating, and implementing actions to perform counter narratives against attitudes and actions of exclusivism, violence, and intolerance. The religious and youth leaders engage in public to condemn violence and call for respect for differences and call for peace in their region.

actual.value: Youth and Religious Leader

comment.narrative: The participants for this training are 34 youth leaders and 17 religious leaders. The participants felt they had experienced significant changes in attitudes, such as being more egalitarian, inclusive, and respectful in social interactions became stronger. They can see problems from various points of view, can appreciate differences, and control their ego and emotions in interactions. Apart from that, they are more aware of the importance of discipline, patience and empathy. All of this is the first step towards a wiser, more tolerant, and caring attitude towards others, especially in addressing diversity issues. They admitted that they had increased their skills in lobbying, planning, communicating, and implementing actions, as well as their ability to analyze social dynamics. The youth leaders together with religious leaders were encouraged to continue collaborating in facing the challenges of diversity issues in their respective regions. They are encouraged to organize meetings to build local networks by involving local religious leaders and youth. This meeting aims to explore further the situation of diversity issues in their region and formulate strategies and programs with local networks.

title.narrative: Study on the policy of FoRB and dissemination through discussions, writing a policy paper, press conferences, and seminars.

description.narrative:
YBAW has organized a series of discussions and studies involving experts in the field of FoRB, and the results were then compiled into a paper that will be used as a reference for advocacy and gathering public support.
The first discussion was held on May 8, 2023, in Jakarta with issue mapping and reviewing several research studies by several institutions such as the Wahid Foundation, Setara Institute, and INFID. The discussion then explained several findings from FGD results in the field that had been carried out by the Gusdurian Network in various regions (Semarang, Gorontalo, Brebes, Mojokerto, Sukabumi), as well as the results of social media monitoring regarding FoRB cases.
We then wrote the results of the study into a policy brief document, which we then discussed at a consultative meeting on August 26, 2023, in Yogyakarta, involving experts as reviewers. In general, the policy brief highlights several FoRB problems, including discriminatory regulations, weak law enforcement officials facing intolerance and a lack of prevention efforts, intolerant groups that are increasingly aggressive, media that is biased in discriminating against minority groups, and victim groups that experience fear.

comment.narrative: YBAW will organize this activity by involving experts in the field of FoRB to discuss and compile a policy paper that will be used as the basis for advocacy and to garner public support.

target.value: Policy paper

comment.narrative: CSO activists and religious actors who are involved by duty-bearers in the policy-making process: such as in planning programs, or solving problems related to intolerance, or participating in consultations regarding policies related to FoRB. A paper describing context, regulatory framework, analysis and recommendations for policies related to FoRB.

actual.value: Policy Brief

comment.narrative:
YBAW with several CSO develop the policy brief highlights several FoRB problems, including discriminatory regulations, weak law enforcement officials facing intolerance and a lack of prevention efforts, intolerant groups that are increasingly aggressive, media that is biased in discriminating against minority groups, and victim groups that experience fear.
The following are several recommendations that YBAW have highlighted as a result of the study and need to be followed up in the future: a) At the policy level, state policies and regulations must be oriented towards strengthening freedom of religion and belief as mandated by the constitution.
b) Citizenship education that strengthens the perspective of equality and freedom of religion and belief. This action was carried out in various spaces, both cultural and structural, especially in educational institutions (schools, Islamic boarding schools, seminaries, and others). At the grassroots level, cross-stakeholder collaboration is needed to create meeting spaces that erode the barriers of exclusivism between citizens.
c) At the network level, civil society groups collaborate to strengthen the mainstreaming of tolerance at various levels.
